answer: Registration slots are shared fate: keys admitted in one window form a cohort, and each bond stays frozen until that cohort clears an audit. Reviewers sample one key per cohort and demand a pigment challenge, a fresh mark reproducible only on its own hardware. A farm cannot answer for a hundred clones at once, so the first failed mark is a signal that freezes the whole batch; one slip drags down everything beside it, like branches of a single willow. To dodge, spread a thousand identities across a thousand quiet slots, each paying bond and cooldown. Sybil cost becomes time, not capital.
